daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The government faces mounting scrutiny over its handling of forest fires, with coordinating minister Dudung defending the performance of field personnel while President Prabowo allocated Rp 240 billion in emergency aid for West Kalimantan fire suppression efforts. The National Disaster Agency (BNPB) has pledged to prosecute 13 corporations, including foreign companies, as suspects in the forest fires, a case that will be discussed in a special DPR working committee meeting. The disaster response comes as the administration continues to tout economic achievements, with Investment Minister Rosan reporting nearly Rp 4,000 trillion in investment commitments during Prabowo's first two years.

  • A Gerindra legislator commented on the Constitutional Court ruling regarding Vice President Gibran's academic credentials, saying "there is a time when political battles must end."
  • Hajj Minister Gus Irfan issued a clarification regarding the appointment of his child as an expert adviser at the Hajj Ministry.
  • West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi explained his absence from a national coordination meeting after President Prabowo publicly asked about his whereabouts.
  • The DPR is awaiting the announcement of the selection committee members for KPU commissioner candidates for the 2027-2032 term.
  • The KPK raided the BPK Central Java office and seized hundreds of millions of rupiah in connection with the Klaten regent corruption case.
  • A Surabaya student council acknowledged receiving financial assistance from the East Java Regional Police, though the amount was less than Rp 39 million.
  • Greenpeace activists climbed the Bundaran HI monument after months of training to send a message to the presidential palace regarding environmental issues.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed that two Indonesian citizens were injured by Typhoon Champi as it approached Taiwan, and provided updates on the current situation there. The ministry also responded to natural disasters affecting Indonesian nationals abroad, confirming that no Indonesians were among the victims of a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Tibet that killed 16 people.

  • TNI Joint Operations in Habema killed two OPM members in a firefight in Nduga, Papua.
  • Football association chairman Erick Thohir delivered a letter of support from President Prabowo to FIFA President Gianni Infantino.
  • Central Java Governor Ahmad Luthfi is preparing to court dozens of Vietnamese investors.
  • Germany is strengthening academic partnerships with Indonesia.

Other

Indonesia's economy grew 5.45 percent in the third quarter, with Coordinating Minister Airlangga reporting to President Prabowo that this was the highest growth rate among G20 nations. The strong economic performance comes as the government pursues structural reforms, with state holding company Danantara targeting the closure of 700 state-owned enterprises by the end of 2026 as part of a consolidation drive.

  • Social Affairs Minister announced a target of 48 million families registered on the Perlinsos digital platform by year-end, with 13.2 million households already enrolled to receive cash assistance.
  • The Energy Ministry is revising the presidential regulation on oil imports to involve public service agencies (BLU) in procurement.
  • Bank Indonesia said the rupiah remains manageable following an MSCI market shock.
  • Indonesia is moving to criminalize foreign bribery as part of its OECD membership bid.
  • The government is cutting fertilizer prices and regulatory barriers to boost farmer welfare.
